Post Date: 2016-09-08T14:31:02Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: skipUntil with "empty" observable causes source obs to never complete.
Description: Hello,

``` java
Observable.interval(1, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
      .doOnNext(n -> Timber.d("firstObs %s", n))
      .doOnUnsubscribe(() -> Timber.d("onUnsubscribe"))
      .doOnCompleted(() -> Timber.d("onCompleted"))
      .skipUntil(Observable.timer(3, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
        .flatMap(b -> Observable.empty())
        .doOnCompleted(() -> Timber.d("onCompleted2")))
      .subscribe(
        n -> Timber.d("Next? %s",n),
        e -> Timber.d(e, "Err"),
        () -> Timber.d("Completed")
      );
    Timber.d("Ciao");
```

Looking at this snippet I would expect "Completed" to be triggered upon skipUntil observable completion ('after 3 seconds'). 

After some time of debugging I found out it's not the case and the Source observable does not get "onCompleted" or "onUnsubscribe" called when the latter `skipUntil` obs completes its execution.

This means that the first obs is never gonna end and the emitted items are not going to reach the end of the chain

llm_response:
CATEGORY: 1
REASONING: This issue can be analyzed without a build environment. The problem is conceptual and relates to the behavior of RxJava's `skipUntil` operator when combined with an empty observable. The issue describes how `skipUntil` with an empty observable causes the source observable to never complete, which is unexpected behavior. 

The issue can be verified through code analysis: when `Observable.empty()` is used in the `skipUntil` parameter, it completes immediately without emitting any items. According to RxJava's contract, `skipUntil` should start emitting items from the source once the secondary observable emits any item, but since `Observable.empty()` completes without emitting, the source observable never gets a signal to start emitting and thus never completes.

This is a behavioral issue in the RxJava library that can be understood and verified through analysis of the operators' documented behavior and the code logic, without needing to actually build and run the code.
